newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria to privatise power, telecomms - minister.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria to privatise power, telecomms - minister.

text.p: Nigeria's military government plans to privatise its national electricity and telecommunications firms, finance minister Anthony Ani said in an interview published on Monday.
"We are going to privatise NEPA (National Electric Power Authority) in all its ramifications," he told Thisday newspaper.
"We are going to privatise NITEL (Nigerian Telecommunications Limited) wholesale but we are going to invite international private telecommunications companies to do it," he added.
The remarks were the clearest sign that Nigeria is set to resume privatisation of public enterprises, embarked upon in the late 1980s as part of a structural adjustment programme (SAP).
General Sani Abacha's government, which came to power in 1993, dumped SAP wholesale the following year but has since 1995 being implementing what it terms "guided deregulation."
The World Bank and Nigerian businessmen have been advocating that privitisation should resume in order to revive the economy now that key macro-economic sectors have been stabilised.
Ani said modalities were being worked out to make the sale of NITEL and NEPA open and competitive. "The whole world must see Nigeria to be transparent, we have to do things the way they should."
He did not say when the sale would commence but it is widely expected that details will be announced in next year's fiscal budget broadcast of Abacha due to made in January.
Nigeria, Africa's most populous nation of 100 million, fell into trumoil in 1993 when the army annulled a presidential vote that would have restored democracy.
Abacha's government is undertaking a programme of transition to civil rule aimed at handing over power in 1998 although his critics say it is a ruse to perpetuate his rule.
But it has succeeded in reducing inflation, stabilising exchange and interest rates and stopping budget deficits through an economic programme that is being praised by the World Bank.
